sentences.text: A boat at a dock is usually held by four or more lines.
The bow line runs forward from the bow, and the stern line runs aft from the stern, both holding the boat in to the dock.
The bow spring runs from near the bow aft to the dock and stops the boat surging forward, while the stern spring runs from near the stern forward and stops it moving back.
A breast line runs straight across to hold the boat close.
Leave slack for the tide, or the boat can hang from its lines as the water falls.
